clue.text: Castle left to Bill in Scotland

definitions.text: Castle left to Bill in Scotland

indicators.note: the first piece is placed to the left of, that is before, the second

parts.note: a castle is a fortified stronghold, a fort
Bill is the pet form of the name William

explanation.surface: A will bequeaths a stronghold to someone called Bill north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left to' reads like a bequest, but it places the castle piece to the left of Bill's full name. FORT WILLIAM is a town in the Scottish Highlands, named after a fort.
explanation.definitionFit: The town takes its name from a garrison built there in the Highlands, so a stronghold named for a William fits a Scottish place.

clue.text: Ornamental fastenings covering chess piece could be found in the pond

definitions.text: could be found in the pond

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of, covering, the second

parts.note: frogs are decorative braided loops and toggles used to fasten coats
a pawn is the lowliest chess piece

explanation.surface: Decorative buttons wrapped around a chess piece might turn up in a garden pond.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumps of jelly-coated eggs laid by amphibians are a familiar sight floating in garden ponds each spring.

clue.text: Flashy airmen, swimmers

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force, Britain's airmen
fish are creatures that swim

explanation.surface: Showy pilots go for a swim.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffish describes someone rakishly showy or disreputably stylish, a near synonym of flamboyant.

clue.text: At which point our nephew cracked up

indicators.note: the words are broken apart and reassembled, as something cracked into pieces would be

explanation.surface: The moment when someone's sister's son burst out laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked up' suggests laughter, but it shuffles OUR NEPHEW.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb introduces what happened immediately after, meaning at that moment or upon which.

clue.text: Prone to being dishonest

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is reclining horizontally, the other is telling fibs; the same word covers both.

clue.text: Not right in previous part of play

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-husband
a play is divided into acts

explanation.surface: Something mistaken in an earlier section of a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means imprecise or not quite correct, so not right fits.

clue.text: Snake by degrees round Bond's boss

indicators.note: the two degree abbreviations go around, enclosing, the spy chief's letter

parts.note: MA (Master of Arts) and BA (Bachelor of Arts) are university degrees
MA (Master of Arts) and BA (Bachelor of Arts) are university degrees
M is James Bond's boss in the spy novels and films

explanation.surface: A serpent gradually coils around the head of the secret service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by degrees' looks like 'gradually', but it means two academic degrees, MA and BA, placed round M.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a fast, venomous African snake.

clue.text: Alcoholic evidence

definitions.meaning: ... is the scale measuring the alcohol strength of spirits, as in 70 ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a measure of spirit strength and demonstration that something is true.

clue.text: Plain vegetation?

parts.note: seems to mean ordinary greenery, but 'Plain' is a flat grassland, and the South American plains have a famous tall ornamental grass

explanation.definitionFit: The tall feathery grass is named after the pampas, the vast grassy plains of South America.

clue.text: It's to do with the skin at start of rubella outbreak that's going round

definitions.text: It's to do with the skin

indicators.note: the outbreak word goes round, enclosing, the single letter

parts.note: an epidemic is an outbreak of disease

indicators.note: the first letter of the word rubella is taken

explanation.surface: A rash-causing disease spreading through the community affects the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' fits an infection spreading, but it puts R inside EPIDEMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The epidermis is the outer layer of skin, and the adjective describes anything relating to it.

clue.text: An obvious benefit

parts.note: clear means plain to see
profit means gain or advantage

explanation.surface: A plain advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Net gain after all costs is an unmistakable financial advantage.

clue.text: Bulky lump I have

parts.note: a mass is a lump or solid body
contracted to I've

explanation.surface: Someone reports carrying a large lump.
explanation.definitionFit: Massive means large and heavy, a synonym of bulky.

clue.text: Change imperceptibly when jazz does not start in the entrance

indicators.note: the shortened jazz word goes inside the entrance word

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

indicators.note: the jazz word loses its opening letter

parts.note: trad is short for traditional jazz

explanation.surface: Things shift subtly when the band at the door doesn't strike up.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAD without its first letter gives RAD, which sits inside GATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To gradate is to pass by gradual stages from one shade or quality to another.

clue.text: An area between Skegness and Hunstanton, having surface covered with water

parts.note: the Wash is the square bay on the east coast of England between these two seaside towns

explanation.surface: A stretch of English coast is flooded.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a broad tidal estuary on England's east coast; Skegness (Lincolnshire) and Hunstanton (Norfolk) are resorts on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: Awash means flooded, with water lying over everything.

clue.text: Piece-worker!

parts.note: suggests someone paid by the item, but reads as someone working only a portion of the hours

explanation.definitionFit: A person employed for only part of the working week works a piece of the full time.

clue.text: Oxide that's unusual on this planet

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: rare means uncommon
Earth is the planet we live on

explanation.surface: A compound that is scarce here on our world.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare earths are the oxides of the lanthanide metals, a group of chemical compounds.

clue.text: Little 18 company of five make a fuss about raw sugar

parts.note: 18-down is MUSICAL; 'Little' asks for its short form, mus.
V is the Roman numeral for five
ado means fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A small troupe of five performers kick up a fuss about unrefined sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscovado is an unrefined dark brown cane sugar.

clue.text: Does he take part in the arms race?

definitions.text: Does he take part in the arms race?

parts.words: Does he take part in the arms race?
parts.note: an arms race is nations stockpiling weapons, but read literally it is a race involving arms, and the smuggler runs guns

explanation.definitionFit: An arms smuggler runs guns illegally, so is literally a runner in a race of weapons.

clue.text: One French drink perhaps that's out of the ordinary

parts.note: un is French for one
a regular's usual drink at the bar is 'the usual'

explanation.surface: A Frenchman orders a drink that turns out to be odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Unusual means uncommon, outside normal experience.

clue.text: Ebenezer had no end to unhappiness

indicators.note: the last letter of the unhappiness word is dropped

parts.note: misery is deep unhappiness

explanation.surface: Ebenezer's unhappiness was endless.
explanation.walkthrough: Ebenezer Scrooge is the tight-fisted hero of Dickens's A Christmas Carol, the archetypal skinflint.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge is literature's best-known hoarder of money, so his first name stands for a skinflint.

clue.text: Show of harmony?

definitions.meaning: relating to melody and harmonious sound

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a song-and-dance stage production and an adjective for anything melodious.

clue.text: Attack a sailor soundly

indicators.note: the phrase is judged by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, said together as 'a salt'

explanation.surface: An attack on a sailor is thoroughly carried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'thoroughly', but it signals that 'a salt' (a seaman) is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent attack.

clue.text: Quietly put on mat finish with gesture of indifference

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
a rug is a mat

explanation.surface: Someone softly lays a finishing touch on a mat with a dismissive gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrug is a raising of the shoulders that signals not caring.

clue.text: Animal turns tail in Ethiopia

indicators.note: only the last pair of letters of the animal is turned round

parts.note: a tiger is a big cat

explanation.surface: A creature flees in East Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns tail' means flee, but here the last two letters of TIGER swap places. Tigre is a people and language of Ethiopia and Eritrea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigre names a people and language of the Horn of Africa found in that country.

clue.text: Slightly reduce fees oaf arranged

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy lout sorts out charges, cutting them a little.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to lessen or relax somewhat.

clue.text: Con urges another revolutionary leader to become a beggar

indicators.note: the letters are made into another arrangement
the first letter of the word revolutionary is taken

explanation.surface: A trickster incites a second rebel chief to go begging.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrounger cadges things from others, a sponger or beggar.

clue.text: Main map

parts.note: the Main is a poetic name for the open sea, so a map of the sea is meant

explanation.definitionFit: Navigators use a nautical plan of coasts and depths when sailing the open sea.

clue.text: Most valuable greeting for a new member of staff

definitions.text: Most valuable greeting for a new member of staff

parts.note: gold is the most precious metal, hence golden
hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: A precious welcome given to a recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump-sum payment offered to attract a new recruit when joining a company.
